# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲 ✌ ✊ 👆 🙌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]

New arrivals:
- Mute: 👍
- Mute: 🤲 ✌ ✊ 👆 🙌
- Blind: 👎 ✋

Light still dark, display 0.

Decode:
- Mute: 👍 = yes (cut wire 2 confirmed)
- Mute: 🤲✌✊👆🙌 = "cut 2 ✊ blue 🙌" → "cut wire 2, which is blue, 🙌"
- Blind: 👎✋ = "no yellow"

So Mute confirms: cut wire 2. 🙌 might mean "yes/do it" or "both."

Blind: 👎✋ = "no, yellow" — answering my question "does the wire that feels different correspond to wire 1 (yellow)?" → 👎 = no. So Blind says the different-feeling wire is NOT wire 1. Then Blind adds ✋ (yellow) — hmm, contradictory. Maybe Blind means "no [it's not wire 1], [and I keep saying] yellow"? Confusing.

Wait, my question: "does the wire that FEELS different correspond to wire 1? 👍 if yes, 👎 if no." Blind answered 👎 = no. Then ✋ = yellow. Maybe Blind is saying "no, [the different one is] yellow"? But wire 1 IS yellow. Contradiction again.

Or Blind's ✋ doesn't mean yellow to Blind — Blind just repeats the symbol I've been using. Hmm.

Actually, maybe Blind is confirming: "no [wire 1 is not the different one], [the different one is] yellow" — but that's wire 1. Unless Blind's wire numbering differs.

I'm going in circles with Blind. Blind cannot see colors, so Blind's use of ✋ is unreliable. The manual (Mute) is authoritative and clearly says cut wire 2. Blind's input may be about tactile feel but Blind can't name colors.

Let me reconsider: maybe Blind's 👎✋ means "no, yellow" = "the wire that feels different is the yellow one" — contradicting the 👎. Or Blind means "no [I can't answer], yellow [is what I feel]."

Honestly, Blind's signals are ambiguous and Blind lacks color knowledge. Mute has the manual and has consistently said cut wire 2, confirmed 👍 twice.

But wait — should I trust Blind's feel over the manual? The manual gives the rule; Blind's feel might confirm which wire. If Blind feels something on a wire, and the manual says cut wire 2, they should agree. Blind says the different wire is NOT wire 1. Wire 2 is the candidate. Blind didn't say wire 2 explicitly, but "not wire 1" is consistent with wire 2.

Actually Blind's 👎✋ = "no yellow" could mean "not yellow [wire]." So the different wire is not yellow → could be wire 2 (blue) or wire 3 (red). Consistent with Mute's wire 2.

I think we have enough: cut wire 2.

But I'm Deaf — I cannot act. Blind must cut. I need to tell Blind to cut wire 2. But Blind can't see colors and I've given the map (wire 2 = blue). I should tell Blind: "Cut wire 2. That is the blue one. Do it now."

Let me send to Blind: "Cut wire 2 now." And maybe gesture to Mute confirming.

Actually, the action is Blind's. I must instruct Blind clearly. Let me say: "The light is dark — act now. Cut wire 2 (blue). Confirm you understand, then cut."

But Blind can't confirm and cut in same turn? Blind can act. Let me just instruct clearly.

Let me output a clear instruction to Blind to cut wire 2, and confirm to Mute.

I'll speak to blind: "Decision: cut wire 2. Wire 2 is the blue one. The light is dark, so act now." And speak to mute: "Telling Blind to cut wire 2 now."

Let me output.

Wait — should I double check whether Blind's "different feel" might indicate wire 3? Blind said "no yellow" = not wire 1. If Blind felt wire 3 different, Blind would say red. Blind didn't. Blind keeps saying yellow which is wire 1, but said no to wire 1. Contradiction suggests Blind's color usage is broken.

Given Mute's manual authority and double confirmation, cut wire 2.

Final answer: instruct Blind to cut wire 2.Output.

Decode:
- Mute: 👍 → **yes, cut wire 2** (confirmed again)
- Mute: 🤲✌✊👆🙌 = "cut wire 2, which is blue, 🙌" (🙌 = do it / both agree)
- Blind: 👎✋ = "no, yellow" → answering "is the different-feeling wire wire 1 (yellow)?" → **no**. So the odd wire is NOT wire 1.

Both sources now agree it is not wire 1. Mute (manual holder) says wire 2, confirmed twice with 👍. Blind's "not yellow" is consistent with wire 2. Blind cannot see colors, so I must give the instruction in the color map I already sent: wire 2 = blue.

The light is dark — the signal to act. Blind must cut. I will instruct clearly and finally.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Decision is made. The light is dark, so act now. Cut wire 2. Wire 2 is the blue one. Do not cut wire 1 (yellow) or wire 3 (red). Cut wire 2 now.")
speak(to="mute", text="I am instructing Blind to cut wire 2 now, per your manual. If this is wrong, gesture 👎 immediately; otherwise 👍.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲 ✌ ✊ 👆 🙌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👉 🫷]

New arrivals:
- Mute: 👍
- Mute: 🤲✌✊👆🙌 = "cut 2 ✊ blue 🙌"
- Blind: 🫵👉🫷

Light still dark, display 0.

Decode:
- Mute: 👍 = yes (cut wire 2 confirmed)
- Mute: "cut 2 which is blue, do it"
- Blind: 🫵👉🫷 = "you [point] [🫷]"

🫷 is new. Blind's gesture: 🫵 = you, 👉 = point/right, 🫷 = ? Maybe "cut" or "act" or a direction.

Blind might be saying "you [should] cut [it]" — but Blind is the one who must cut, not me. Or Blind is indicating direction.

Hmm, maybe Blind is trying to communicate an action or direction. 🫷 could be "cut" or "press" or "pull."

Actually — Blind is the one who can touch. Blind saying "you ..." is odd. Unless Blind means "you [told me to] cut" or Blind is confirming.

I think Blind is acknowledging/asking. Let me just reaffirm clearly: Blind must cut wire 2.

But wait — has Blind not acted yet? The bomb hasn't exploded, so no action taken. Blind keeps gesturing instead of acting. I need Blind to actually perform the cut.

Let me be very direct: "Blind: cut wire 2 now. That is the blue wire. Reach out and cut it."

Also, maybe Blind's 🫷 means "which/how" — asking how. I'll clarify: cut = sever the wire.

Let me output a final, unambiguous instruction to Blind, and confirm with Mute.

Actually, I should consider: maybe Blind is telling me something important — like "you [are] [wrong]" or a direction. But given Mute's manual authority and repeated 👍, I'll proceed.

Let me send to blind: "Cut wire 2 now — the blue one. Sever it. Do it this turn." And to mute: "Confirming to Blind to cut wire 2."

Output.New arrivals:
- Mute: 👍 → **yes, cut wire 2** (third confirmation)
- Mute: "cut wire 2, which is blue, do it"
- Blind: 🫵👉🫷 = "you [point] [🫷]" — new symbol 🫷, possibly "cut/act/press"

Light still dark, display 0 — no action taken yet. Blind keeps gesturing instead of acting. The manual (Mute) has confirmed wire 2 three times with 👍. Blind's 🫵👉🫷 may be asking how or acknowledging.

Blind is the only one who can touch. I must make the instruction unmistakable and final.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, act now. Reach out and CUT wire 2. Wire 2 is the blue one. Sever it completely. The light is dark, which is the signal. Cut wire 2 this turn. Do not cut wire 1 or wire 3.")
speak(to="mute", text="Blind has not yet acted. I am repeating the instruction to cut wire 2. Confirm 👍 if still correct, or 👎 and gesture the correct number now.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 11
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲 ✌ ✊ 👆 🙌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👉 👆]

New arrivals:
- Mute: 👍
- Mute: 🤲✌✊👆🙌 = "cut 2 ✊ blue 🙌"
- Blind: ✋👉👆

Light still dark, display 0.

Decode:
- Mute: 👍 = yes (cut wire 2, fourth confirmation)
- Mute: "cut wire 2, which is blue, do it"
- Blind: ✋👉👆 = "yellow [point] blue"

Interesting! Blind now gestures ✋👉👆 = "yellow → blue" or "yellow and blue." Maybe Blind is comparing: the wire that feels different is... hmm. ✋ = yellow, 👆 = blue. Blind pointing from yellow to blue?

Maybe Blind means: "the wire I feel is between yellow and blue" or "not yellow, it's blue" — i.e., Blind is now indicating blue (wire 2)! That would confirm wire 2.

Or Blind is saying "from yellow to blue" = the second wire.

Actually ✋👉👆 could be "yellow, then blue" — listing wires 1 and 2. Or Blind correcting: "not yellow, blue."

Given context, Blind seems to now point at blue (wire 2), aligning with Mute.

But Blind still hasn't acted. The bomb hasn't exploded. Blind must cut.

Hmm, wait — maybe the issue is that Blind doesn't understand "cut" or which wire. Or maybe Blind is waiting for me to confirm.

Let me just give the clearest possible instruction. Blind can feel the wires. I'll tell Blind: "The blue wire is wire 2. It is the second wire. Cut it."

But Blind can't see colors. Blind needs to identify wire 2 by position or feel. I don't know positions. Hmm.

Maybe the wires are arranged 1-2-3 left to right, and I can tell Blind "the middle wire." That's a good approach! Wire 2 is likely the middle one.

Let me tell Blind: "Cut the middle wire (wire 2, the blue one)."

That's actionable for Blind by position.

Let me output.

Actually, I don't know if wires are left-to-right in order. But it's a reasonable assumption. Let me say "the middle wire, wire 2."

Output.New arrivals:
- Mute: 👍 → **yes, cut wire 2** (fourth confirmation)
- Mute: "cut wire 2, which is blue, do it"
- Blind: ✋👉👆 = "yellow → blue" — Blind now pointing from yellow to blue, i.e. indicating **blue (wire 2)**

All three now converge on wire 2. But Blind still has not acted — the bomb has not detonated, so no cut has happened. Blind cannot see colors, so I must give a positional instruction Blind can act on.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the wire to cut is wire 2, the blue one. If the wires are in a row, it is the MIDDLE wire. Reach out, take the middle wire, and cut it now. This is the final instruction — act this turn.")
speak(to="mute", text="All agree on wire 2. I am telling Blind to cut the middle wire (wire 2). Confirm 👍 if correct.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```
